title: Primary school De Verwondering
description: De Verwondering is the first of a new generation of school buildings that seek to (re)connect children to nature through its presence in architecture, interior design and landscape. Better learning and more nature awareness in future generations through biophilic and regenerative design.

title: Bienenskulptur
description: The Beesculpture is a space for Bees and Humans. The exterior design shows the negative form of a bee cell and reflects the basic hexagonal structure of bees. The 7 meter high space was built  with sustainable materials in a collaborative effort with many volunteers. A space for contemplation.

title: Nature Retreat Westbroek
description: Designed as a place for urban professionals to reconnect with nature, these biophilic buildings made of wood nudge the occupants to go outdoors. Biobased materials, plenty of daylight, luscious green roofs, and transparent facades blur the lines between the man-made and the natural world.

title: Augstine's Garden
description: Augustine's Garden is a residential ensemble resulting of a transformation of former low-rise industrial buildings in the courtyard of a 1900s quarter. The site is converted into a contemporary urban garden, and the post-industrial aesthetic of the buildings reflects the concept of adaptive reuse.

title: Les promenades d'Icare
description:
Ambitious energy renovation project for 250 homes, using the ENERGIESPRONG methodology for industrial mass building and performance improvement.
The elevation adopts a classic contemporary style. A specific tile is proposed. With a 7 cm exposure, it reinvents the rhythm and vibration of the brick.

location.street: 9 Rue du Dieu de Marcq Lille
9 Rue du Dieu de Marcq Lille

title: Château de Beaucastel
description: At Beaucastel, water, wind, soil, and sun shape an architecture rooted in place, using excavation earth for cellars and walls and a rain-fed cistern that supports winemaking and cools interiors passively. Lime, clay, earth, sand, wood, stone ensure an aging well and self-sufficiency project.

title: Rosa María house
description: Two patios organize a fluid transition between interior and exterior, enhancing light, views, and climate control. Natural materials like lime, pine, and terracotta promote tactility, durability, and circularity through prefabrication and passive design strategies
imageCredit: Paco Marín / aerial photos: Studio cafecito

title: DUCHESSE
description: An existing building and two former industrial halls are transformed into varied housing around a shared green space. The project preserves key heritage elements, enhances natural light and privacy, and promotes community through adaptive reuse and collective outdoor areas.

title: Haus am Ziestsee
description: Reconstruction and extension of a weekend house from the 1920s, at the Ziestsee, in the vicinity of Berlin. The house has been rebuilt in accordance with its original condition and extended with a wooden house. An outbuilding in wooden construction completes the ensemble.

title: Chiericati Enoteca
description: The refurbishment of the Enoteca is the centrepiece of a transformation in which the spatial disposition is adapted to the new challenges of the winery. Embracing self-construction, the project fosters a close connection with the people, the materials of the regions and the reuse of local resources.

materials.supplierName: Lime putty by Calce Piasco and glacial sand from Cava di Molinazzo di Monteggio.

title: Café nomade
description:
Design, planning, and supervision of a participatory project to build a bar for non-profit organisations.
The triply cabinet accommodates all the recycled components: kitchen cabinets, sink, cladding, and refrigerators. The project, carried out with volunteers from was completed over three weekends.

materials.materialName: Lamps and trash can lid made from wood scraps

title: Bademaschinen
description: Bademaschinen lies in the Oslo Fjord and is inspired by the Sjøbadehus with their traditional roof shapes and towers. The primary design driving factor was the reuse of teak window frames from a 1960s nursing home outside of Oslo that was undergoing rehabilitation and conversion into housing.

title: PONT-FARBEL
description: The renovation project involves the installation of a central load-bearing wall made of TERRAPAD and partitions made of TERRAPLAC, as well as HAGA BIOTHERM insulating plaster made of lime and cork. Several elements have been reused, such as doors, joists and exterior paving.

title: natural kindergarten
description: Renovation of a barn in a natural kindergarten with natural materials, wood, lime etc.

title: Passive House in Serra d'Ordal
description: House in Serra d'Ordal combines bioclimatic strategies, natural materials, and sustainable solutions to create a net-zero home with minimal environmental impact. Near Barcelona, it features a bioclimatic patio, cross ventilation, rammed earth walls with cork insulation, and renewable energy systems.

location.street: Carrer Sant Joan de la Salle
Carrer Sant Joan de la Salle

title: Zurich Bus Station
description: Because of the short life-span of the building (max. 10 yrs.) we chose a simple woodframe construction with mineral insulation. No internal claddings, only visible installations. Facade of painted 3-layer woodboards, protected by a steel canopy. The building is designed for easy disassembly.

title: Omloop
description: How to tackle the typical Flemish “Fermette?” After a critical analysis, the answer was found in densifying and reconnecting with the surroundings. Doing so by transforming a part of the roof into a wintergarden and optimizing the existing spaces.

title: Blue House Azores
description: The Blue House is a sustainable retreat in the Azores, built with wooden prefabricated elements and clad in up-cycled ocean plastic, and local carpentry techniques. Blending modern design with local stone and native plants, it exemplifies low-impact architecture in harmony with its coastal setting.

title: The Dialogue Express Cafe
description: Dialogue Express Cafe is run by a social enterprise that creates employment and social opportunities for deaf and hard of hearing persons who take customer orders in British Sign Language. The Cafe is located inside a converted railway carriage outside Stratford Station in East London.

title: The Paper Garden
description: The Paper Garden is an ecology garden and educational building in London built by volunteers using 60% retained, reclaimed + natural materials. The space is used for growing, making, cooking, story-telling and stillness so people can come together and contribute to ecological and social change.

materials.supplierName: The City of London Corporation Forestry Team

title: UDO
description: UDO is versatile standalone micro home suitable for craftsmen’s platform truck. It is constructed around a wooden structure, sustainable insulation and a façade made of reused aluminium. Using the adjustable legs UDO can be placed almost anywhere: on construction sides aswell as in the landscape.

title: 30+8 Social Housing units in Palma de Mallorca
description: The residential project of 38 dwellings combines sustainability, functionality, and a social character. It uses local materials such as compressed earth blocks and timber, reducing the carbon footprint. The spaces are flexible, well-ventilated, and promote community living and energy efficiency.

title: Barretts Grove
description: Barretts Grove by GROUPWORK is a six-flat CLT building with a red brick cladding which serves as a rainscreen and echoes the surrounding buildings. The CLT superstructure is left exposed, obviating the need for other finishes or unnecessary details and reducing the embodied carbon by 20%.

title: Chalet Dahu - Low-impact hempcrete self-build
description: Family self-build project inspired by the local, vernacular architecture. Entirely breathable building envelope. 40 cm thick hempcrete walls. Solar panels. Electric energy for heating. Large openings for passive solar gain on south and west facades. Minimises synthetic materials (< 3% of volume).

title: Joli
description: The house echoes the former holiday home, with generous windows framing marsh, garden, and sky. In a compact spatial composition, each room connects uniquely to the landscape. Built from prefabricated wood and straw bales finished with clay, it’s a low-energy home made from sustainable materials.

title: The Makers Barn
description: Once an abandoned piggery, now a fine example of elemental architecture, The Makers Barn goes to great lengths to honour its agricultural origins. Borrowing its robust pitched roof from the nearby Tudor cottages and clad with vertical larch planks, against a meadow of tall grasses and wildflowers.

title: After-School Care Centre Waldorf School am Prenzlauer Berg
description: The existing school was energy-retrofitted and extended with a after-school care centre that contrasts the existing structures. The design is rooted in regional, renewable materials: timber construction with straw insulation and clay plaster. Green roofs and minimal technology complete the concept.

materials.materialName: Wood: Timber, Larch, Pine, White Fir

title: The Gallery House
description: Shifting from gallery to house, suggested without determining space as footprint and ecological considerations, form the topic the project. Purified details, based on a “countryman’s logic” lead to a self-evident simplicity and readability of the architecture seemingly ‘belonging’ to the landscape.

materials.materialName: Natural Calque Plaster and Natural Calque Paint

title: Kiosk zur FÜRstin
description: Make do with what is. The kiosk consists of 90% reused building material that were obtained directly from the surrounding mayor construction site – its offcuts, its demolition waste or the trees that had to make way. We built without using any cement or fresh concrete.

title: Gemüseeck – Center for Bioregional Architecture
description: The Gemüseeck is a center for bioregional architecture, providing an environment for learning and prototyping regenerative building materials: geo-based, bio-based and re-use. This project frames a new holistic social practice and an economy of commoning for the rural region of Uckermark.

title: Lake House Bad Saarow
description: The intent was to create a sustainble and contemporary house for a young familiy with two children. The house is located right at the shore of a lake and is surrounded by a big natural garden. It is primarily constructed from timber, making up the main material of its structure and all over cladding

title: Building Beyond Bricks
description: Created by Building Beyond Borders students of Hasselt University with local support, the project features a pavilion and earth oven in an abandoned vicarage’s garden in Belgium. Built with bio-based, geo-based, and reclaimed materials, the project showcases inclusive, sustainable architecture.

stakeholders.companyName: Building Beyond Borders postgraduate certificate 2023-2024, UHasselt

title: House without any cement
description: A very small house, built without cement or adhesives. Foundations are solid granite blocks. Prefabricated timber walls filled with hempcrete, which insulates and wraps the building, plastered with lime. This "neo-timber-frame" method minimizes thermal bridges and uses natural, sustainable materials

title: office  Van Laethem - Architecten
description: Our Tiny Office is a functional but compact, serene workspace built from mainly wood, hempcrete and rammed earth. Natural materials and minimal tech reflect our vision for sustainable design proving that eco-conscious building enhances comfort and atmosphere, and does not limit it.

title: Inhabiting the stable
description: The project involves converting a disused rural section of a farm into an apartment. The living area occupies the former hayloft, while the bedrooms and bathroom are located in the old stables. The combination of old walls and more recent brick additions enhances the didactic quality of the space.
